subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord plugin-owned bot self-profile mutation surface, and should it use a new Discord-only `self-profile`/`selfProfile` contract or the existing `set-profile` action pattern?
rationale: This would create a public config/action surface that mutates Discord bot identity through stored credentials, so automation should not choose the authorization, account-routing, validation, audit, naming, and partial-failure contract alone.

options.title: Approve narrow self-profile contract
options.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off, self-only profile action with explicit account selection, avatar validation, tests, docs, and live Discord proof, reusing `set-profile` naming if maintainers want cross-channel consistency.

options.title: Keep presence-only scope
options.body: Leave nickname/avatar mutation out of OpenClaw for now and route only status/activity needs through the existing presence action or the open dynamic-presence API discussion.

options.title: Defer identity mutation model
options.body: Leave Discord bot identity changes manual or external until maintainers define a broader identity model across self-profile, per-binding identity, and webhook persona delivery.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-profile contract
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off, self-only profile action with explicit account selection, avatar validation, tests, docs, and live Discord proof, reusing `set-profile` naming if maintainers want cross-channel consistency.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest shipped Discord presence-health work and explicitly documented that it did not add self-profile behavior.
